_comment: Recorded identities of the primary constellation toolchain, for S0 D5.
Each entry binds a NAME to a source COMMIT and the SHA-256 of the binary
attested to have been built from it. The commit is the identity; sha256 is
what makes the attestation checkable afterwards, so a binary swapped on
PATH later is caught. `version` is recorded ONLY so a gate record can show
what the binary claims about itself -- it never accepts or refuses.
The three oracles come from THREE DIFFERENT repos; do not assume one.
md and mk recorded 2026-08-14; both repos were verified clean at the
commit below at the moment of recording.
ms re-recorded 2026-08-15 at the ms-cli-v0.16.0 RELEASE TAG, whose target
commit is d49d5c09. F-177's scheduled bump: S5 extends the oracle, so the
S0 re-anchor happens once rather than twice. Note the tag is the release
identity and it is one CI-only commit BEHIND mnemonic-secret's master
(6fdfd36); the tag is what is pinned.
checkout_clean_when_recorded is FALSE for ms, and the previous `true` was
wrong -- this very comment said the tree was dirty and 'is marked' while
the flag read true. The flag is recorded conservatively: the reference
checkout /scratch/code/shibboleth/mnemonic-secret carried 3 untracked
files and sat at master, not at the pinned tag, when this was recorded.
The binary itself was built by `cargo install --path crates/ms-cli
--locked` from a dedicated `git worktree` detached at d49d5c09, whose own
`git status --porcelain` was empty -- so the bytes came from a clean tree
AT the pinned commit, and the flag understates rather than overstates. The
sha256 below was shown to be independent of the build directory: two
worktrees at different paths produced byte-identical binaries.
Re-record with scripts, not by hand, when any oracle is rebuilt:
sha256sum ~/.cargo/bin/md
git -C /scratch/code/shibboleth/descriptor-mnemonic rev-parse HEAD
